title: Benefiber vs up&up Clear Dissolving Fiber (Wheat Dextrin)

brand.product: Benefiber Daily Prebiotic Fiber Supplement Powder, Unflavored, 17.6 oz (125 servings)

alternative.product: up&up Clear Dissolving Fiber Supplement Powder, 17.6 oz (125 servings)

summary: Both are a single-ingredient powder of wheat dextrin giving 3 g of soluble fiber per 2-teaspoon serving, 125 servings per 17.6 oz tub.
evidence: The NIH DSLD label for Benefiber powder (GSK, 500 g/17.6 oz) lists 3 g soluble fiber per 4 g (2 tsp) serving and 'Other ingredients: Wheat dextrin' only. Target's up&up listing lists wheat dextrin as the only ingredient, 3 g soluble fiber per 2 tsp, 15 calories, 125 servings per 17.6 oz.
differences: Some older up&up reviews and Q&A mention a corn dextrin formula; the current listing says wheat dextrin, so check the label on the tub you buy. Several reviewers report clumping after a formula change. up&up is labeled gluten-free (<10 ppm).

aspects.brand: Wheat dextrin only; label says gluten-free and non-GMO
aspects.alternative: Wheat dextrin only; Target says wheat processed to meet FDA gluten-free rules
Older listings and reviewers mention corn dextrin and a formula change; reviews report clumping

title: Citracal Petites vs Equate Calcium Citrate + D3 Petites

brand.product: Citracal Petites Calcium Citrate with Vitamin D3, 200 coated caplets

alternative.product: Equate Calcium Citrate + D3 Petites Tablets, 200 count (Compare to Citracal Petites with Vitamin D3)

summary: Both give 400 mg of calcium as calcium citrate plus 500 IU vitamin D3 per 2-tablet serving, in small 'petite' tablets.
evidence: NIH DSLD label for Citracal Petites (Bayer) shows calcium 400 mg and vitamin D 12.5 mcg per 2-caplet serving. Walmart's Equate listing shows 400 mg calcium citrate and 12.5 mcg (500 IU) D3 per serving, 2 tablets twice daily, and carries the claim 'Compare to Citracal Petites with Vitamin D3 formula'.
differences: Inactive ingredients and coating may differ. Both bottles are 200 count (50-day supply at 4 per day).

title: Emergen-C Immune+ vs Equate Vitamin C Plus Vitamin D & Zinc Packets

brand.product: Emergen-C Immune+ Vitamin C Drink Mix, Super Orange, 30 packets

alternative.product: Equate 1000 mg Vitamin C Plus Vitamin D & Zinc Powder Packets, Orange, 30 count (Compare to Emergen-C Immunity+)

summary: Equate's packet is sold as a direct 'Compare to Emergen-C Immune+' copy: 1000 mg vitamin C with vitamin D, zinc and B vitamins per packet.
evidence: NIH DSLD shows Emergen-C Immune+ (30 packets) at 1000 mg vitamin C, 25 mcg D3, 10 mg zinc, B6 10 mg and B12 25 mcg per packet. Walmart's Equate listing confirms 1000 mg vitamin C plus vitamin D, zinc and 7 B vitamins and the 'Compare to Emergen-C Immunity+ Ingredients' claim, but its supplement panel was not readable, so D and zinc amounts are not independently confirmed.
differences: Emergen-C Immune+ includes a 500 mg proprietary complex (larch arabinogalactan, yeast beta-glucan); we could not confirm whether Equate includes it. Flavor differs. Check the Equate panel for D and zinc amounts.

title: Nature Made Vitamin D3 2000 IU vs Spring Valley Vitamin D3 2000 IU

brand.product: Nature Made Vitamin D3 2000 IU (50 mcg) Softgels, 250 count

alternative.product: Spring Valley Vitamin D3 Softgels, 50 mcg (2,000 IU), 400 count

summary: Both are one-a-day softgels with 50 mcg (2000 IU) of vitamin D3.
evidence: Walmart listings for both products state 50 mcg (2000 IU) vitamin D3 per softgel. Nature Made 250 ct is $14.52 (5.8 cents each) and Spring Valley 400 ct is $9.38 (2.3 cents each).
differences: Carrier oil and softgel ingredients were not listed on either page. Nature Made is USP Verified; we did not confirm third-party verification for Spring Valley.

aspects.alternative: No USP seal on the Spring Valley D3 labels found; independent verification not confirmed
Soybean oil, gelatin, glycerin, corn oil (found label is the 1000 IU version, 2018)

title: Nature Made Melatonin 5 mg vs Spring Valley Melatonin 5 mg

brand.product: Nature Made Melatonin 5 mg Extra Strength Tablets, 90 count

alternative.product: Spring Valley Melatonin Tablets, 5 mg, 120 count

summary: Both are plain 5 mg melatonin tablets, one at bedtime.
evidence: Target's Nature Made listing shows 5 mg melatonin per tablet (other ingredients croscarmellose sodium, magnesium stearate), $8.99 for 90. Walmart's Spring Valley listing states 5 mg melatonin per tablet, 120 servings, $6.24.

title: Glad ForceFlex vs Kirkland Signature Flex-Tech 13-Gallon Trash Bags

brand.product: Glad ForceFlex 13-Gallon Drawstring Tall Kitchen Trash Bags, 110 count

alternative.product: Kirkland Signature Flex-Tech 13-Gallon Kitchen Trash Bags, 200 count

summary: Kirkland Flex-Tech bags are thicker and held more weight than Glad ForceFlex in Reviewed's load test, at about a third less per bag.
evidence: Reviewed.com loaded bags with dumbbells in 5-lb steps: Kirkland Flex-Tech held 35 lb versus 30 lb for Glad ForceFlex 13-gal. Today.com's two-month hands-on test lists Kirkland at 0.9 mil versus Glad at 0.72 mil, but scored Glad higher overall (4.5 vs 3.3), with Kirkland feeling slightly damp after a milk-leak test.
differences: Mixed results: Kirkland won on load strength and thickness, Glad won on leak resistance, snug fit and odor control in Today's test, and Kirkland's drawstring cinches less tightly. Kirkland needs a Costco membership. Glad's Febreze scent version is priced here.

aspects.brand: Leak 5/5, odor 4.5/5, overall 4.5/5; no wetness after milk test
aspects.alternative: Leak 3/5, odor 4/5, overall 3.3/5; bag 'a tad moist' after milk test
Drawstrings could not cinch as tightly as other bags
